content: Triggers on the acoustic drums fire samples. The 808 bass drum sounds of Threshold are triggered by the kick drum. On tour the triggers were less reliable on rented kits than on the band's own kit. Crowder also uses the Evans Hybrid Sensory Percussion system; it is set up again at each show.
parameters: Roland RT series triggers on the drums. Pintech RS-5 piezo trigger on hi-hat or stack. Sensory Percussion Sound System, version 2

content: Sensors on the acoustic drums read where and how the drum is hit. Software maps each zone and type of stroke to samples or synth controls.
parameters: Standard product knowledge; not confirmed in a source

content: A Roland SPD-SX PRO sample pad, sent to the mixer in stereo. It also holds a backup click and backup copies of the backing tracks. Earlier: Roland SPD-SX that also drove video (2016); Roland Octapad (2012).
parameters: 1 pad unit; 2 output channels; 1 backup click

item: Laptop with Ableton Live and click tracks
content: The show runs from a laptop with Ableton Live: backing tracks, click, sections that loop, and sections that wait for a cue. Two Live sets run and connect by Ethernet across the stage. The drummer hears his own click with many subdivisions; the other players hear a simpler click; a third click from the sample pad is the backup. Reported faults: an automatic update during a soundcheck; one extra beat added in a song in 7/8. One reviewer felt that the click made the first piece drag.
parameters: Ableton Live 11 (gear page). 2 Live sets. 3 click channels. 2 channels of tracks to the mixer
source: neely-eu22; neely-eu24; neely-grind; neely-iem22; crowder-gear; ha-interview; postmusic-live25

content: All sources go to the band's own rack mixer. Each player sets a personal in-ear mix that is the same each night. In-ears remove the delay of sound through air.
parameters: Sources 2022: 8 drum microphones, stereo sample pad, stereo tracks, stereo bass, bass synth, sax, stereo keys, voice, 3 clicks, audience microphone. Mixer: PreSonus 24R (24 channels, 2022), PreSonus 32R (32 channels, 2024). Sound through 50 feet of air and back: about 100 ms

item: Three octave pedals on the bass
content: On the title track of the 2024 album the bass uses three octave devices. (1) Three Leaf Audio octave pedal, Tim Lefebvre signature: warm, like a synth, tracks well; his usual tour pedal. (2) Boss OC-2: tight, staccato, punchy. (3) A bass synth pedal on setting 7 with the 'sens' and 'range' knobs at zero: tracks very fast and very low, with a grimy sound.
parameters: 3 octave devices. Pedal 3 cost about 50 dollars and is much louder than unity
where: Against the Fall of Night (title track)

item: Model names of two bass pedals (estimate)
content: The captions do not give clear model names. The Three Leaf Audio signature pedal of Tim Lefebvre is the Octabvre. A bass synth pedal with seven settings and 'sens' and 'range' knobs agrees with the DigiTech Bass Synth Wah.
parameters: Estimate; not confirmed in a source

content: Line 6 HX Stomp (later HX Stomp XL) for amp models, reverbs and distortions. Eventide H9 for reverbs and effects. Wireless: Line 6 Relay G70, later a Shure unit. The bass runs in stereo: a large octave sub sound, with a stereo chorus that fills the sides and moves across the speakers. He wants less than about 5 ms between the pluck and the sound.
parameters: Latency limit about 5 ms. 2 bass channels. 1 modeller + 1 multi-effect + 1 to 3 octave pedals

content: In the 2012 dubstep remix the bass 'wobble' was played live with pitch bend and a motion ring (Source Audio Hot Hand). Nothing was programmed. The electronic percussion was played on a Roland Octapad.
parameters: 2013 pedal list: Source Audio BEF Pro with Hot Hand, ZVex Mastotron fuzz, Boss OC-2, Boss LS-2, EHX Iron Lung vocoder, Line 6 M13

content: The piano intro of Sequence Start was played by a Disklavier, a Yamaha piano that plays from MIDI. The 2014 credits name iPad synthesizers (Crowder) and programming (Neely). A 2016 live video uses an iPad glitch effect. A curator describes the early sound as 'mainly driven by glitch sound effects, bass, guitars and drums'.
parameters: 1 MIDI piano; iPad synths; glitch effect
source: tvdb-seqstart; neely-covers; bc-vol1; wiki-disklavier; tvdb-iwalk; musicto-iwalk

content: Sounds of old game consoles are in the music from the first EP. Reviews name an '8-bit chorus' (Threshold), an '8-bit' album close (Cytherean), chiptune keys (Hot Saturn) and 'chip jazz'. Neely describes this taste in a 2015 lesson: contemporary harmony with 'obnoxious sounds'.
parameters: Console styles named: Super Nintendo, Sega Genesis. 3 tracks with chip sounds named in reviews
source: larsen-perihelion; bluesuns-atfon; bc-perihelion; ha-interview; allthethings-atfon; tvdb-8bit

content: A looped voicemail message is the base of Thicc. The track Perihelion starts with vocal loops. Reviewers hear pitched vocal snippets in vaporwave style and 'distorted, almost androgynous vocals'. Neely teaches the vocoder on bass and uses autotune in his theme music.
parameters: Voices on 4 of 10 tracks (2021); 0 of 9 tracks (2024)
source: larsen-perihelion; xisuma-perihelion; bc-perihelion; tvdb-vocode; tvdb-quartal; bc-atfon

item: Sound features of the electronic styles named in the sources
content: Features that the encyclopedia articles give for each style, for the sound design of a section.
parameters: Dubstep: sub-bass; bass with volume, distortion or filter moved by a low-frequency oscillator (wobble). Drum and bass: syncopated breakbeats; deep sub-bass; 808-style bass drum. Future bass: filter wobble; risers of pitch above white noise before a drop; arpeggio chords; vocal chops; vocoders. Trap (EDM): 808 drum samples; bass drops; build-ups and breakdowns. Glitch hop: chopped samples; stutter effects; distorted bass lines. Vaporwave: slowed samples; chopped and screwed; much reverb
source: wiki-dubstep; wiki-dnb; wiki-futurebass; wiki-trap; wiki-glitchhop; wiki-vaporwave

content: 6 of 8 tracks have a Moog bass with the electric bass. Bigly Strictness: a second player doubles the bass line on Minimoog. Xavi: the Moog doubles the bass in the choruses only. Bad Kids to the Back: a keyboard player takes the bass on Minimoog in the choruses.
parameters: Moog bass by the bass player on 2 tracks; by a keyboard player on 4 tracks

content: Tarova: electric bass and Moog Sub Phatty by one player. Grown Folks: electric bass and 2 Moog bass credits. GØ: a keyboard player has the Moog bass. Big Ugly: Moog bass and no electric bass.
parameters: Synths on the album: Minimoog, Moog Sub Phatty, Prophet 6, ARP Omni, ARP Axxe, Synthex, Mellotron, vocoder, talkbox

content: On stage League plays some bass parts on a Moog Little Phatty or a Moog Sub Phatty with 25 keys. On Empire Central he plays Minimoog Model D bass on 2 tracks. On Bigly Strictness he uses a pick and 2 octave pedals.
parameters: Electric bass: Fender Precision (1959) with flatwound strings .045-.105. Pedals: 2 octave pedals, delay, phaser, envelope filter, fuzz

content: Forum users connect the sound with a Korg KingKORG. They hear almost the same sound for the lead from about 5:40 until a preset change at 8:20. One user thinks that he changes the amount of LFO to the filter cutoff. A different user thinks that he uses only the joystick and no pedal.
parameters: 2 presets in the lead part of the solo. These are opinions of forum users, not a statement by the player
where: Lingus (film of We Like It Here)

content: Bill Laurance: Fender Rhodes, Nord Stage, Moog Little Phatty. Justin Stanton: Fender Rhodes, Prophet-6, Minimoog Model D, Mellotron. Shaun Martin: Korg Kronos, Moog Little Phatty with talkbox, Mellotron, vocoder. Bobby Sparks: Minimoog Model D, Hammond B3, Hohner D6 clavinet with a whammy bar.
parameters: 3 to 4 instruments for each player. An analogue delay pedal (MXR Carbon Copy) on the Little Phatty, the Rhodes, the Minimoog, and the Kronos

content: Prophet-6: a 'buzzy' lead on What About Me?; filter moves make a sound brighter or darker. Minimoog: mainly bass, sometimes lead; it has no presets, thus the player makes each sound live. Nord: an electric grand piano like the Yamaha CP-70.
parameters: Bass = Minimoog; lead = Prophet-6 or Minimoog; strings and pads = Mellotron or ARP String Ensemble (from the rig lists)

content: A Moog synth feeds the talkbox. Sleeper has a talkbox solo. Fuel City starts with a talkbox melody. Mean Green has vocoder textures. On Culcha Vulcha he plays only vocoder and talkbox.
parameters: Signal path: synth - amplifier - speaker driver - tube - mouth - microphone. On Empire Central a tight microphone (LS-208) is on the talkbox
where: We Like It Here; Culcha Vulcha; Empire Central
source: storm-rigs; albumism-wlih; storm-empire; liner-culcha; wiki-talkbox; lauten-empire

content: Bobby Sparks plays the clavinet with a whammy bar and pedals. On Chonks his clavinet solo goes through a guitar amplifier head (Supro Statesman); many listeners thought that it was a guitar solo.
parameters: Clavinet solos with whammy bar also on RL's, Mean Green, and Chimera

content: The band uses Danelectro baritone guitars 'all the time'. One tune has 2 baritone guitars tuned to A; a different baritone is tuned to B. Strat-type guitars are the usual sound of the band. The amplifiers on tour are Supro.
parameters: Baritone strings .013-.068. Overdrive always on with low gain; fuzz into an overdrive for a thick sound like a synth; delay; chorus set as vibrato

content: Trumpet solos with a wah pedal and other effects. A tenor sax solo with fuzz. On Grown Folks one tenor solo has effects and the next tenor solo is clean. A muted trumpet on The Simple Life. On Lingus a processed trumpet trades with the synth.
parameters: 2 horn colours for solos: processed and clean
where: Culcha Vulcha; Empire Central; Somni; We Like It Here

content: Few electronic sounds. Only the bass drum has a trigger.
parameters: Trigger module (Roland TM-2); clap and 808 samples; analogue drum synth clone (Pearl Syncussion, 2 channels, no presets). Multi-effect (Eventide H9): timed delays, compression, distortion

content: The engineer changes the sound of the band in real time.
parameters: "I control the input, he controls the output." The band plays with in-ear monitors only

content: An analogue poly synth for bass, pads and textures; software synths for sound design.
parameters: Prophet-10 (bass); Prophet X from 2018; Omnisphere, Keyscape and Massive from 2016. Drum pads (Nord Drum 3P) in one video: weak evidence

content: One software synth and one sampler make most sounds.
parameters: Massive: "The only synth I've ever used". Sampler loops of microseconds as synth tones. Piano and string libraries. No analogue synths and no outboard effects

content: Each pad plays a chain of samples. The sound moves on with each hit.
parameters: 24 pads; song structure in the arrangement view; program changes switch the synth sounds; the drum programs were made on the computer first and then learned

content: Small MIDI keyboards and stock software.
parameters: Gear page: GarageBand and Massive; 49-key MIDI keyboards; Pro Tools for some mixing; SM57 on the snare in one video. Interview: his demos are distorted, lo-fi, made of MIDI sounds

content: Two common electronic effects. No source for these artists was found.
parameters: Side-chain: kick lowers pads and bass by 3 to 10 dB; release 100 to 250 ms. Bit reduction: 8 to 12 bits; sample rate 11 to 22 kHz (estimate)

content: Both bands played for years through digital amp modellers direct to the PA with no speaker cabinets.
parameters: Animals as Leaders: a Fractal Axe-Fx II made every guitar tone on The Joy of Motion and on stage. Meshuggah: Axe-Fx units with the tempo of each song stored in the patch; a laptop with Cubase changed the patches during the show

content: Both guitarists have a signature plugin that holds the full chain: pedals, three amps, cabinet responses, delay and reverb.
parameters: Archetype: Abasi: clean amp with a piezo-like blend, tight high-gain rhythm amp, lead amp with boost; compressor for thumping; drive pedal; 9-band EQ; digital delay; reverb; more than 70 cabinet impulse responses. Archetype: Plini: clean, crunch and lead amps; bus-type compressor; octaver (one octave up and one down); drive; chorus; delay with tape saturation; reverb; doubler; transpose of up to 12 semitones

content: Drums are often programmed first and replaced or doubled later. Samples support the real kit on the records.
parameters: First Animals as Leaders album: drums and synthesizer effects programmed by the producer. Catch Thirtythree: all drums programmed. obZen: live drums with Drumkit from Hell samples as a second sound source. Meshuggah demos: full programmed drums in Cubase. The Joy of Motion: first Animals as Leaders album with real drums on all tracks
source: wiki-abasi; wiki-aal; wiki-meshuggah; wiki-obzen; pg-hagstrom-2017; pg-aal-2014

artist: Animals as Leaders; Plini; Tigran Hamasyan
content: Guitar bands add an electronic layer through a guest or the producer. Hamasyan plays the synthesizers himself and uses a synth lead for a solo.
parameters: Electronics production by Navene Koperweis (2014). Synthesizers by Machinedrum on one track (2016). Synth arrangement by Misha Mansoor (2022). Piano and synthesizer by Dave Mackay and by Anomalie for Plini. Hamasyan: synth solo in 'Double-Faced' over a 4/4 groove; drummer with live electronics
source: wiki-joy-of-motion; wiki-madness-of-many; wiki-parrhesia; bc-plini-iv; bc-plini-sunhead; wiki-mockroot; eguez-2020

content: Pitch effects extend the range of single notes in a riff or thicken chords. A looper can change speed and octave.
parameters: Whammy pedal with MIDI automation for one or two notes at a time. Octaver for 'crunchy' chord progressions. Looper trick: record a multi-tap delay figure at half speed, then play it at normal speed: one octave higher and twice as fast, like wind chimes

content: Early electric keyboards. The Solovox and the Clavioline play one note at a time, with a reedy whine. He plays one of them with one hand and the piano with the other hand.
parameters: Hammond Solovox (3 octaves, mounted under the piano keyboard): acquired 1941; on a recording of 29 July 1948. Wurlitzer electric piano: on a recording of 12 July 1956. Selmer Clavioline (records of 1963 to 1967): vacuum-tube oscillator; buzzy wave that is almost square; high-pass and low-pass filters; vibrato; about 3 octaves; invented 1947
where: Deep Purple; Jazz by Sun Ra; Cosmic Tones for Mental Therapy; The Magic City; Heliocentric Worlds Vol. 2

content: New names for stock instruments. He plays the organs with fists and elbows to get clusters.
parameters: Hohner Clavinet = "Solar Sound Instrument" (recorded 1967-68): slow vamps over percussion. Gibson Kalamazoo organ ("Solar Sound Organ" in the credits): organ solo of about 15 min (1967). Farfisa organ: on a record of early 1970; on 4 of 5 tracks of Space Is the Place (1972)
where: Atlantis; My Brother the Wind Vol. II; Space Is the Place

content: A transistor electric piano with a tone like a harpsichord. It is the main keyboard of a quartet record.
parameters: Rock-Si-Chord Model 100: introduced 1967; 2 voices (string, lute); sound from oscillators, with no strings. Quartet record of 1970. Concert of 17 December 1971: exchange between the Minimoog (one note) and the Rocksichord (chords)
where: The Night of the Purple Moon; Nidhamu

content: He gets a Minimoog before the instrument is on sale.
parameters: 1969: demonstration of the Moog modular by Gershon Kingsley in New York. Autumn 1969 (probably October): Moog lends him a prototype Minimoog (Model B), the third or fourth made. March 1970: the Model D goes on sale. 1970: a second Minimoog. Sources give August 1969 or 2 November 1969 for the first Moog recording
where: My Brother the Wind; Space Probe

content: Two Minimoogs at the same time give two voices. The sounds are noise and sweeps, not tunes.
parameters: Minimoog: 3 oscillators, noise source, 24 dB/octave low-pass filter, 44 keys, one note at a time, pitch wheel. Sounds: bloops, slow portamento, blasts of white noise, clusters together with the organ. Solos of 17 to 20 min. In 1979: 3 synthesizers at the same time

content: A ring of keyboards around the player, with effect units.
parameters: By mid-1970: Clavinet, Kalamazoo organ, Farfisa, Rocksichord, Minimoog, piano. Festival credits of 1970: Farfisa, Clavinet, piano, Rocksichord, Spacemaster organ, Minimoog, Hohner Electra. Effects: echo repeaters, tremolo, phaser, distortion. Studio of 1978: ARP, Rhodes, Minimoog, Hammond organ
where: It's After the End of the World; Lanquidity

content: An organ with a built-in drum box and a simple bass line. The drummer plays with the machine.
parameters: Milan, 23 January 1978; quartet (keyboards, tenor sax, trumpet, drums). Rhythm box: a slowed-down cha-cha beat with a synthesized bass line. Title track: 26 min

content: The electric piano goes through a tape delay and a wah pedal. He changes the echo time while he plays.
parameters: January 1971. Echoplex: tape delay (first made 1959; solid-state EP-3 from 1970) with a moving head, so the delay time can change in real time. Also a pitch shift that gives a wobble. Used in the intro, on lines from 1:00, and at the peak of the solo

content: Funk keyboard with fuzz, wah, and echo. Rhodes through a ring modulator.
parameters: Credits: Hohner D6 Clavinet with Fender Fuzz-Wah and Echoplex; electric bass with wah-wah and fuzz; kazoo. Ring-modulated Rhodes in Rain Dance and from about 11:00 in Hornets. Mellotron on Hidden Shadows (tapes of about 8 s for each key)

content: A synthesizer player adds an "electronic orchestration" to finished band tracks.
parameters: Early 1972; Moog III modular; 16-track tape. About half of the album overdubbed in about 24 hours. First sound: like a flock of birds that rises out of the music. Sources name Quasar or Water Torture as the first track

content: A synthesizer with patch cords and no memory, played live in a jazz septet.
parameters: 20 to 35 patch cords; about 300 patch changes in one night; 10 to 20 patches in 4 to 5 minutes. With sample-and-hold, wah pedal, and Echoplex. ARP 2600 (made 1971-1981): 3 oscillators, 24 dB/octave low-pass filter, ring modulator, noise, spring reverb

content: A random note pattern from a sample-and-hold circuit is recorded. One part of it is chosen and looped. Bass and drums play with the loop.
parameters: Two ARP 2600 at the same time. "Random Resonator" box with a knob for the amount of randomness. Name on the tape box: "Loop Tune". Length 9:16. Low synthesizer drones under the bass solo

content: The bass line is a synthesizer, not a bass guitar.
parameters: ARP Odyssey: 2 oscillators, 2 notes at a time, 37 keys; the model of 1972-75 has a 2-pole filter. The line was recorded alone, to a click, several times with different sounds. Two sounds were layered. One later article names a Minimoog

content: A preset lead synthesizer for solos. The Clavinet plays the part of a funk rhythm guitar.
parameters: ARP Pro Soloist: 30 presets, 37 keys, 1 oscillator, key pressure for vibrato, bend, and brightness. Synthesizer solo of about 3 min (sources name the Soloist or the Odyssey). Clavinet D6: 60 keys, 60 strings, 2 pickups, 6 rocker switches

content: From one electric piano to a set of ARP instruments and a vocoder.
parameters: 28 December 1967: first electric piano at a session. 1971: Rhodes only. 1972: Mellotron; Moog (Gleeson). 1973: ARP 2600, Pro Soloist, Clavinet, Odyssey. 1974: ARP String Ensemble (49 keys, full polyphony, triple chorus, no filter). 1978: Sennheiser VSM-201 vocoder on 3 tracks
source: sos-hancock; wiki-mwandishi; wiki-crossings; wiki-sextant; wiki-thrust; wiki-solina; wiki-sunlight

content: The electric piano goes through a ring modulator for a whirring sound.
parameters: Middle section of Seventh Arrow (recorded 16 February 1971). Concert in Tokyo, 13 January 1972: prepared electric piano and ring modulator, with no synthesizer. Other effects on the Rhodes: phase shifter, Echoplex, wah-wah
where: Weather Report (1971); I Sing the Body Electric

content: The synthesizer comes in first for sound effects, then for melodies and solos. Two units with different sounds can be coupled.
parameters: November 1971: sound effects on Unknown Soldier. 1973: melodic lines. From about 1973-74: solos. "Eins": soft and clean. "Zwei": harder edge. 3 oscillators each; coupled and detuned: 6 oscillators for chords (1974). No presets
where: I Sing the Body Electric; Sweetnighter; Mysterious Traveller

content: The control voltage of the keyboard is inverted. High keys give low notes.
parameters: Mirror about C: C and F-sharp stay; B becomes C-sharp; B-flat becomes D; A becomes E-flat. The right hand plays the theme on the inverted keys. The left hand plays normal chords on the Rhodes. For the solo he sets the keyboard back to normal

content: A lead for one note at a time, like a folk wind instrument.
parameters: ARP 2600; attack like a woodwind; constant LFO modulation of the fine tuning of the oscillator; no pitch wheel in use (both hands on keys). He compares the tone to his accordion with felt glued inside

content: The first polyphonic synthesizer of the band, for reed-section and string sounds.
parameters: First on Heavy Weather (1977); Four Voice or Eight Voice (sources differ). Each voice is one module with 2 oscillators and a 2-pole filter (low-pass, band-pass, high-pass, notch); each voice is set by hand. Zawinul: it sounds like a big reed section. It doubles the bass line of Teen Town
where: Birdland; A Remark You Made; Teen Town

content: A polyphonic synthesizer with memory, and a vocoder for melodies.
parameters: Prophet-5: shown January 1978; 5 voices, 2 oscillators for each voice; 44 programs of his own; first on Mr. Gone (1978). Korg VC-10 vocoder: melody of 8:30 (1979). Stage of 1978: 2 ARP 2600, Rhodes, Oberheim, Prophet-5, Mu-Tron Bi-Phase, volume-wah

content: A lead synthesizer played with the pitch wheel like a string instrument. The model for the bends is the South Indian veena.
parameters: First on record: August 1972. Sawtooth wave. Oscillator 3 modulates the filter cutoff at a rate near audio frequency (a "buzzing" tone). Right hand on the keys; left hand on the pitch wheel. Bend range of his first Minimoog: a fourth; two semitones are too few for him. Often through a distorted guitar amplifier. Before: Rhodes with ring modulator

content: Lead synthesizer doubles the guitar. Solos use more and more pitch bend.
parameters: 1974: first synthesizers; solos overdubbed on Minimoog over one-chord bass vamps. 1976 track: square-wave pulse from the Polymoog with LFO on the filter at 0:16; Minimoog doubles the guitar line at 0:18 with a little portamento; solo from 4:21; large upward bends at 6:18
where: Where Have I Known You Before; Duel of the Jester and the Tyrant

content: One or more sine waves with no overtones. The sub sits under the mid-bass, and the kick sits above the sub.
parameters: Fundamental about 30 to 60 Hz (one octave); sub-bass register in general: about 20 to 70 Hz; clean sine at 25 to 80 Hz; best notes F to A in the lowest octave; two sines one octave apart through a low-pass filter; grime "sublow" lines often near 40 Hz

content: An LFO moves the cutoff of a low-pass filter on a long bass note. The LFO can also move the volume or the distortion.
parameters: LFO locked to the tempo; rate 1/8 note in one patch and dotted 1/8 in another; a sine LFO is smoother than saw or square; 24 dB low-pass; mono; notes C2 to C3; release 570 ms; the rate can be automated

item: Wobble rates in Hz at 140 BPM
content: One LFO cycle for each note value.
The LFO rate changes at a beat or at a half bar.
parameters: Typical bar: 1/4 for two beats, then 1/8, then 1/8 triplet or 1/16 on the last beat; the fastest rate comes before the bar line. Estimate

content: A silent oscillator modulates the frequency of the carrier. One LFO moves the amount of FM and a filter at the same time.
parameters: LFO on: high-pass cutoff, resonance, carrier level, FM amount. Square-wave sub on its own low-pass filter. Then chorus, compression and distortion. Skrillex used the FM8 synthesizer; Noisia showed it to him in 2010
where: Tutorial patch; Scary Monsters and Nice Sprites

content: The ratio is the frequency relation of two operators. Integer ratios give harmonic sounds. Other ratios give bell and metal sounds.
parameters: 880 Hz on 440 Hz = 2:1; a modulator one octave down = 0.5:1; modulation at 20 Hz and above is audio-rate

content: Low integer ratios with a moving FM amount.
parameters: Ratios 1:1, 2:1, 3:1 and 0.5:1; FM amount moved by an LFO at a rate of 1/8 to 1/16 note. Estimate

content: The dubstep drop commonly has a wobble bass or a "vowel" bass. Two filter peaks at the formants of a vowel make the bass speak.
parameters: Formants F1 and F2 of a male voice in Hz: i 240 and 2400; e 390 and 2300; a 850 and 1610; o 360 and 640; u 250 and 595

content: Record the bass to audio and use the audio as a new source.
parameters: Bounce one long note (8 bars at C3) from three patch variants and load it into a sampler. Or freeze and flatten the sub part, process it with heavy distortion and filters, and cut it into short chops

content: Several detuned voices make the bass raw (the Reese method). Mono mode with notes that overlap gives glides.
parameters: Two saw waves 15 to 30 cents apart in one pad example; legato and portamento on

content: The position in the wavetable moves during the note.
parameters: Sweep from an LFO, an envelope or a macro; one sweep for each note of 1/4 to 1/2 beat. Estimate

content: One oscillator into a resonant low-pass filter with an envelope. The notes come from its own sequencer.
parameters: Sawtooth or square wave; low-pass 24 dB per octave, resonant; made 1981 to 1984

item: Detuned bass from techno and jungle
content: A thick bass with slow movement. Dubstep makes it from several detuned voices. Future garage uses a warm, filtered form.
parameters: First use: Kevin Saunderson (as Reese), "Just Want Another Chance", 1988, on a Casio CZ-1000
where: Jungle; drum and bass; future garage
